text.p: The following are the main stories from Thurday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel renews offer to talk with SPD about starting date for planned tax reform
- Trade unions protest against Chancellor Helmut Kohl's appeal to save more and accept pay freezes
- Rumours drive the dollar up to over 1.69 marks. Industry is pleased with low mark-dollar rate
- DIW economic research institute says wages in eastern Germany should not go up any more. Eastern Germany is beset by low productivity
- Health reform is nearly complete, Kohl's ruling coalition discusses amendments and parliamentary groups decide on these on February 18

- Consumer figures still do not show any clear direction. Ifo economic research institute says the climate is bad. But manager of Frankfurt spring fair, Michael Peters says consumer climate is better than feared
HANDELSBLATT

- Finance Minister Theo Waigel offers compromise on tax reform plans. Angry exchange determined mood on Ash Wednesday as Waigel offered the SPD chance to discuss the reform planned to go ahead in 1998 again
- Currency markets challenge G7 countries. Dollar goes above 1.69 marks but slips back after Bundesbank statement

- Growth has its basis abroad. The outlook for German retialers remains poor. The biggest food products retailer, the Rewe group, seeks new growth possibilities abroad. Its acquisition of Austrian Billa group is important step
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl wants to be asked to stand again as chancellor in 1998 general elections. As head of the Christian Democrats (CDU) he says he will only stand in election if "obliged" to. He will decide by CDU party congress in October
- There could be gap of billions of marks in pension funds for former post officer workers
- Kohl's call to accept pay freeze is criticised by trade unions and SPD
DIE WELT
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel makes SPD offer over government's planned tax reform

- Siemens is about to undergo historical restructuring. Chairman Heinrich von Pierer will address annual general meeting for shareholders in Berlin, and is expected to say that unprofitable activities must be pruned
- Kohl calls for acceptance of pay freezes, prompting massive protest from unions
